title: Romaine Caesar Salad with Garlic Croutons
summary: A classic Caesar salad with crunchy garlic croutons and a creamy, anchovy-spiked dressing built on mayonnaise rather than raw egg, for a safe and reliably thick result.
equipment: salad spinner or clean tea towels

ingredients.item: ciabatta or day-old crusty white bread, cut into 2 cm cubes
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
anchovy fillets in oil, drained, patted dry and mashed to a paste
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
romaine hearts (about 2), cut into 2 cm strips

steps.title: Bake the croutons
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Toss the bread cubes with the olive oil, grated garlic and a pinch of salt, spread on a baking tray and bake for 12-15 minutes, stirring once, until golden and crisp all the way through. Cool on the tray so they stay crunchy rather than going soft in their own steam.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice, mashed anchovy, garlic and mustard powder together in a bowl, then whisk in the mayonnaise, grated cheese, olive oil and pepper until smooth and pourable. Building the dressing on halal-certified mayonnaise rather than a raw egg yolk gives the same thick, clinging body safely, with no risk from uncooked egg. Taste and add a little more lemon juice if you'd like it sharper.

steps.title: Wash and dry leaves
steps.text: Wash the romaine hearts and dry them very thoroughly in a salad spinner or tea towel, then cut into 2cm strips. Any water left clinging to the leaves stops the thick dressing from coating them evenly, so it's worth taking this step slowly.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Just before serving, toss the romaine with the dressing in the large bowl until every piece is coated, then add the croutons and toss once more. Scatter over the cheese shavings — check the pack for an animal-rennet-free hard cheese — and a final grind of pepper, and serve immediately so the croutons stay crisp.

tips: Dry the romaine thoroughly — any water left on the leaves stops the thick dressing from coating them properly.
Bake the croutons until crisp right through, or they'll turn soft once tossed with the dressing.
Mash the anchovies to a smooth paste so they disperse through the dressing rather than turning up in chunks.
Check the label for an animal-rennet-free hard cheese if that matters to your guests.
Dress only what you'll eat straight away; leftover dressed leaves go soft within the hour.
storage: Keep the undressed leaves, dressing and croutons in separate containers. The dressing keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days, the croutons stay crisp in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, and the washed leaves keep in the fridge for a day or two. Combine only just before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
